page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-56 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 56 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 28 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is configured with 224 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPU hardware, meaning all storage requirements must be fulfilled via network-attached volumes.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 25%. The PassMark memory score ranks in the top 10%, reflecting highly efficient memory subsystem performance, which is further supported by top-tier text generation speeds for small-scale language models. However, single-core execution speeds, such as Geekbench single-core and gzip compression, fall within the average tier, indicating that workloads relying heavily on single-threaded performance may experience moderate throughput.

From a resource density perspective, the c2d-standard-56 offers a balanced hardware profile that delivers strong multi-threaded compute and memory bandwidth without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. The lack of bundled local storage represents a tradeoff, requiring external storage configurations that may impact overall I/O latency. This instance is well-aligned with multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, database operations, Redis deployments, and medium-scale language model inference.
